models.readme_content:
--- license: apache-2.0 language: - en - es - pt - de - fr - zh - ja - ru - ko pipeline_tag: audio-to-audio tags: - speech - full-duplex - speech-to-speech - haru --- # Haru-4B [Code](https://github.com/higurashi-ai/Haru) · [Technical blog](https://blog.higurashi.ai/melte/haru4b/) · [Technical blog (Japanese)](https://blog.higurashi.ai/melte/haru4b-ja/) Haru-4B is a low-latency and multilingual full-duplex continuous spoken dialogue foundation model: it listens and speaks at the same time, the way people do on a phone call. It is a pretrained base model, released for research. - **Native full-duplex at 7.5 Hz.** Every 133 ms the model takes one frame of the user's audio and produces one frame of its own audio and text. User audio, model audio and model text are summed into a single position of the language model, so listening and speaking never wait for each other. - **Continuous audio, one sampling step.** Audio is a 64-dimensional latent per frame. A small MLP head with MeanFlow sampling produces it in one step from the language model's hidden state; there is no separate audio transformer and there are no discrete audio tokens. - **Character and voice control.** A text card sets the character, a short reference clip sets the voice. - **Multilingual.** English, Spanish, Portuguese, German, French, Chinese, Japanese, Russian and Korean.

## Usage The code is at : a PyTorch implementation with a web demo, an MLX implementation with a native macOS app, and a plugin for serving with vLLM-Omni. With an NVIDIA GPU (about 12 GB of memory): ```bash git clone https://github.com/higurashi-ai/Haru && cd Haru pip install -e ./haru python -m haru.server --hf-repo higurashi-ai/Haru-4B ``` Open , pick a character, give the model a voice, and talk. For low latency, we recommend wired headphones and a wired microphone. Bluetooth devices add 100 ms or more. **Bring your own voice.** Haru ships without voice clips. Upload or record a clip of the voice the model should speak with: one speaker, 3 seconds to 3 minutes, clean speech. Only use voices you have the right to use. ```python from haru import DuplexSession, HaruModel from haru.audio import load_audio, prepare_reference model = HaruModel.from_pretrained("higurashi-ai/Haru-4B") voice = prepare_reference(load_audio("voice.wav")) session = DuplexSession(model, system_prompt=card, reference=voice) frame = session.start() # the model's first 133 ms: frame.audio, frame.text while not frame.done: frame = session.step(user_audio) # 3200 samples at 24 kHz in, 3200 out ``` The system prompt is a character card with a fixed layout; the repository's README shows how to build one. ## Files | File | Contents | | --- | --- | | `model.safetensors` | All weights (bfloat16): `lm.*` language model, `model_audio_proj.*` / `user_audio_proj.*` audio input projections, `head.*` MeanFlow head, `codec.*` audio codec | | `config.json` | Model configuration | | `tokenizer.json` | Text tokenizer | ## Architecture | Part | Details | | --- | --- | | Language model | Qwen3.5-4B text backbone, 32 layers, hidden size 2560 | | Audio codec | VibeVoice acoustic tokenizer, causal, 24 kHz, 3200 samples per latent | | Audio head | 4-layer MLP, MeanFlow, 1 sampling step, guidance scale 1 to 2 (default 1.5) | | Frame rate | 7.5 Hz | ## Limitations Haru-4B is a pretrained base model, released for research. It holds a natural conversation, but it is not a reliable source of facts and does not follow instructions the way an assistant does. It can imitate the voice of a reference clip; only use voices you have the right to use. ## License The weights are released under the Apache License 2.0.

--- ## Table of Contents - [Model Introduction](#model-introduction) - [Pretrained model capability](#pretrained-model-capability) - [Practicality and Cost Efficiency](#practicality-and-cost-efficiency) - [Optimization Approach](#optimization-approach) - [Task Performance and Cost](#task-performance-and-cost) - [User Blind Evaluation](#user-blind-evaluation) - [Appendix: Benchmark results](#appendix-benchmark-results) - [News](#news) - [Model Links](#model-links) - [Quickstart](#quickstart) - [Transformers](#transformers) - [OpenAI-compatible API](#openai-compatible-api) - [Deployment](#deployment) - [DFly2 for Speculative Decoding](#dfly2-for-speculative-decoding) - [Quantization](#quantization) - [Inference Frameworks](#inference-frameworks) - [vLLM](#vllm) - [SGLang](#sglang) - [Finetuning](#finetuning) - [License](#license) - [Contact Us](#contact-us) ## Model Introduction **Hy4 flash** is our most cost-effective Hy model to date, featuring 220B total parameters (including 64B Engram parameters) with just 12B active parameters per token. It natively accepts text and image inputs, generates text, and supports a context window of up to 1M tokens. Its 42-layer language backbone consists of one dense feed-forward layer and 41 MoE layers, with identity Hyper-Connections (iHC) supporting inter-layer information flow. A vision encoder (adapted from SigLIP2-So400m-Patch16-Res512) is connected to the backbone through an MLP projector. In addition to the backbone, a built-in 5-layer drafter, [DFly2](#dfly2-for-speculative-decoding) (0.85B parameters), reuses the target model's KV cache and sparse indices to support long-context speculative decoding at a low, constant cost. Compared with Hy4, Hy4 Flash introduces three notable architectural changes: 1. **Hybrid attention.** Sparse attention (IndexPool) and sliding-window attention (SWA) are interleaved at a 1:3 ratio. 2. **LatentMoE.** Routed experts operate in a lower-dimensional latent space. Each token activates 16 of 512 routed experts, alongside one shared expert. 3. **N-gram embedding (Engram).** The backbone is augmented with learned bigram and trigram representations, retrieved via multi-head hash lookups. | Property | Value | | --- | --- | | **Overview** | | | Architecture | Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) | | Total Parameters (excluding Engram, ViT, and DFly2) | 155.5B | | Engram # FastFrames: Video Generation at Interactive Latency

[![Project Page](https://img.shields.io/badge/Project-Page-green)](https://apple-aiml-research.github.io/ml-fastframes/)
[![arXiv](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2611.23226-b31b1b.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23226)
[![FastFrames-S](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97_Model-FastFrames--S-yellow)](https://huggingface.co/apple/FastFrames-S)
[![FastFrames-L](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97_Model-FastFrames--L-yellow)](https://huggingface.co/apple/FastFrames-L)
[![Community Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97_Space-Community_Demo-blue)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/akhaliq/FastFrames-L)

This repository contains the official implementation of *FastFrames: Video Generation at
Interactive Latency*. We release [FastFrames-S](https://huggingface.co/apple/FastFrames-S)
(1.3B) and [FastFrames-L](https://huggingface.co/apple/FastFrames-L) (14B). Both are
autoregressive, two-step video diffusion models that generate 480p video at interactive
latency. We also release an optimized version of LingBot 1.3B that is 16x faster than the
official model and allows fluid camera-conditioned control.

- [Latency profiling](#latency-profiling)
- [Interactive demo with LingBot](#interactive-demo-with-lingbot)
- [T2V generation](#t2v-generation)
- [VBench evaluation](#vbench-evaluation)
- [Training](#training)
- [Citation](#citation)

[![FastFrames demo: LingBot camera control with and without FastFrames optimizations](assets/fastframes_demo_preview.gif)](assets/fastframes_demo.mp4)

## Installation

Linux x86-64 with an NVIDIA GPU and a CUDA 12.8-compatible driver. From the repository root:

```bash
uv sync
```

Download FastFrames and third-party weights using the [checkpoint guide](https://github.com/apple-aiml-research/ml-fastframes/blob/main/docs/installation.md#checkpoints).

## Latency Profiling

```bash
uv run python evaluation/latency/benchmark.py ff-s
uv run python evaluation/latency/benchmark.py ff-l --gpus 8
```

Example component timings for **FastFrames-S, 1 GPU, 480p**, with a full KV cache.

| Component | Calls | Latency per call | Total latency |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| DiT evaluation, t=1000 | 1 | 16.1 ms | 16.1 ms |
| DiT evaluation, t=833 | 1 | 16.2 ms | 16.2 ms |
| KV refinement | 1 | 2.2 ms | 2.2 ms |
| Pixel decoder | 1 | 0.9 ms | 0.9 ms |
| **Total** | | | **35.4 ms** (paper: 36 ms) |

See the [profiling guide](https://github.com/apple-aiml-research/ml-fastframes/blob/main/docs/inference.md#profiling) for details and baselines.

## Interactive Demo with LingBot

Complete the [demo setup](https://github.com/apple-aiml-research/ml-fastframes/blob/main/docs/lingbot.md#interactive-demo-13b), then launch one of:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 uv run --extra lingbot --extra demo python apps/lingbot/demo.py --gpus 1
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 uv run --extra lingbot --extra demo python apps/lingbot/demo.py --gpus 8
```

and open `http://localhost:8000`.

## T2V Generation

```bash
uv run python scripts/generate.py --model ff-s --checkpoint-dir checkpoints \
    --prompt "A corgi surfing a wave at sunset" --seed 0 --output outputs/corgi.mp4
```

Outputs 832 × 480 video, 81 frames at 16 fps. Use `--model ff-l` for FastFrames-L.

To generate the videos on our project page (20+ videos):

```bash
uv run python scripts/generate_project_page.py --model ff-s --output-dir outputs/project_page/ff-s
uv run python scripts/generate_project_page.py --model ff-l --output-dir outputs/project_page/ff-l
```

See the [generation guide](https://github.com/apple-aiml-research/ml-fastframes/blob/main/docs/inference.md#generation) for details.

## VBench Evaluation

Follow the [evaluation guide](https://github.com/apple-aiml-research/ml-fastframes/blob/main/docs/inference.md#evaluation) to reproduce Table 1's
Quality / Semantic / Total scores.

## Training

### [Causal Forcing++ -> FastFrames-S](https://github.com/apple-aiml-research/ml-fastframes/blob/main/docs/training.md#causal-forcing---fastframes-s)

FastFrames-S keeps the two-step frame-wise Causal Forcing++ generator frozen and trains the
networks around it.

### [Wan2.1-14B -> FastFrames-L](https://github.com/apple-aiml-research/ml-fastframes/blob/main/docs/training.md#wan21-14b---fastframes-l)

We first distill Wan2.1-14B into a two-step causal model following the Causal Forcing++ recipe,
then train its pixel decoder and KV refinement network as for FastFrames-S. We release all
checkpoints: 1) a causal teacher trained on latents generated by Wan2.1-14B; 2) the
consistency-distilled model; 3) the DMD-distilled model; 4) the final generator, pixel decoder
and KV refinement network.

## Citation

If you find this work useful in your research, please cite:

```bibtex
@article{chou2026fastframes,
  title   = {FastFrames: Video Generation at Interactive Latency},
  author  = {Chou, Gene and Yang, Guandao and Luan, Fujun and Mescheder, Lars and
             Dong, Wei and Richter, Stephan R. and Koltun, Vladlen},
  journal = {arXiv preprint arXiv:2611.23226},
  year    = {2026}
}
```

## License and Acknowledgments

LingBot-World v2 code and weights follow their upstream [CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license](https://github.com/apple-aiml-research/ml-fastframes/blob/main/LICENSE_LINGBOT).
All other FastFrames code is licensed under the [Apple Sample Code License](https://github.com/apple-aiml-research/ml-fastframes/blob/main/LICENSE).
Also see [ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS](https://github.com/apple-aiml-research/ml-fastframes/blob/main/ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS) for third-party code.

We thank the authors of [Wan2.1](https://github.com/Wan-Video/Wan2.1),
[Self-Forcing](https://github.com/guandeh17/Self-Forcing), and
[Causal Forcing++](https://github.com/thu-ml/Causal-Forcing) for releasing their code, on which the
FastFrames code and models build.

--- base_model: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B library_name: peft license: apache-2.0 datasets: - harness-hub/scale800-harbor - harness-hub/harness-adapters - harness-hub/termgrade-train-harbor - ai-and/termgrade-environments tags: - trl - grpo - async-grpo - lora - agents - harbor - openenv - pi pipeline_tag: image-text-to-text --- ![](banner.png) A LoRA adapter for [Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B), trained with reinforcement learning to work as the model behind the [pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) coding agent on software-engineering and terminal tasks. > [!Tip] > **Most of the gain of maximum-effort thinking, at a quarter of the tokens.** With thinking off, this adapter > matches the base model thinking at its highest reasoning effort (`xhigh`) on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (56.6% vs 54.2%), > and gets 25 of thinking's 35 points on SWE-bench Pro (64.7% vs 74.5%), while generating about 4.5× fewer tokens per > task. See [Thinking vs no thinking](#thinking). - **SWE-bench Pro (hard 51):** 39.2% → 64.7% (+25.5 points; 15 tasks newly solved, 2 lost). - **Terminal-Bench 2.1:** 39.5% → 55.8% (+16.3 points; 16 newly solved, 2 lost). - **Close to thinking-level accuracy, without thinking:** level with the base model at its highest reasoning effort on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 10 points behind on SWE-bench Pro, with about 4.5× fewer generated tokens. - **Less work per task:** under half the turns of the base model on the tasks both solve. > [!Note] > All results are under the pi harness: one attempt per task, a 100-step budget, thinking off unless stated, text only > (the vision tower is not served), sampling at temperature 0.8 with top-p 1.0 (the training sampling). Base model and > adapter always run under identical settings. These numbers are not comparable with the ones on the > [Qwen3.8-27B card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B), which uses other harnesses (Terminus, Claude Code), > thinking at maximum effort, larger budgets and the full SWE-bench Pro. Full recipe will be shared in [the release blogpost](https://huggingface.co/blog/harness-hub/harness-adapters-at-scale) for anyone to build their own harness adapter. **Pick your setup** [![Results](https://img.shields.io/badge/results-pass%401_%2B_efficiency-555?style=flat)](#results) [![transformers](https://img.shields.io/badge/serve-transformers-ffd21e?style=flat)](#use-with-transformers) [![vLLM](https://img.shields.io/badge/serve-vLLM-30A2FF?style=flat)](#use-with-pi) [![llama.cpp](https://img.shields.io/badge/run-llama.cpp-1f1f1f?style=flat)](#use-with-llama-cpp) [![Llama.app](https://img.shields.io/badge/macOS-Llama.app-7f7f7f?style=flat)](#run-with-llama-app) [![GGUF](https://img.shields.io/badge/download-GGUF-ff9d0b?style=flat)](https://huggingface.co/harness-hub/Qwen3.8-27B-pi-adapted-GGUF) [![Merge](https://img.shields.io/badge/merge-PEFT-ffd21e?style=flat)](#merge) [![Training](https://img.shields.io/badge/training-recipe-4b44c4?style=flat)](#training) [![Trajectories](https://img.shields.io/badge/trajectories-bucket-ff9d0b?style=flat)](#trajectories) A real SWE-bench Pro task under pi: the base model searches and re-runs snippets until it hits the 100-step limit; this adapter finds the function, edits it, runs the tests and fixes the last case, in 8 tool calls. ![](trajectory.gif)
Still version, and the task ![](trajectory.png) Task: `instance_ansible__ansible-d62496fe416623e88b90139dc7917080cb04ce70` from SWE-bench Pro (hard 51), fix `human_to_bytes`. Both runs are from the evaluation above: the base model was graded 0, this adapter 1. Each line is one tool call as the trajectory recorded it, cut to fit.
## Results ![](card-pi.png) | Benchmark | Qwen3.8-27B | Qwen3.8-27B, `xhigh` thinking | **Qwen3.8-27B-pi-adapted** | Qwen3.8-27B-pi-adapted, `xhigh` thinking | |---|---|---|---|---| | SWE-bench Pro (hard 51) | 39.2% | 74.5% | **64.7%** | 74.5% | | Terminal-Bench 2.1 | 41.0% | 54.2% | **56.6%** | 56.6% | On Terminal-Bench 2.1 the four runs are compared on the 83 tasks all of them graded, so the base model and adapter scores differ slightly from the paired results below, which use the 86 tasks those two graded. "Thinking" is the chat template's thinking mode at its default reasoning effort (`xhigh`).
Full paired results (intervals and sign tests against the base model) One attempt per task, thinking off, paired against the base model under pi on the same tasks. The interval is 95%; the p-value is an exact sign test on the tasks that changed outcome. | Benchmark | Tasks | Qwen3.8-27B | Qwen3.8-27B-pi-adapted (step 160) | Difference (points) | Newly solved / lost | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | SWE-bench Pro (hard 51) | 51 | 39.2% | 64.7% | +25.5 ± 14.2 | 15 / 2 (p = 0.0023) | | Terminal-Bench 2.1 | 86 | 39.5% | 55.8% | +16.3 ± 9.1 | 16 / 2 (p = 0.0013) | | Terminal-Bench 2.1, the 68 tasks not used to pick the checkpoint | 68 | 39.7% | 55.9% | +16.2 ± 10.6 | 13 / 2 (p = 0.0074) | - **SWE-bench Pro (hard 51):** the 51 hardest tasks of [SWE-bench Pro](https://huggingface.co/datasets/harness-hub/swebench-pro-v2-hard51-harbor), 2 h and 100 agent steps per task. - **Terminal-Bench 2.1:** all 89 tasks of [Terminal-Bench 2.1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/harborframework/terminal-bench-2.1), 1 h and 100 agent steps per task. Step 160 was picked by looking at the checkpoints' scores on SWE-bench Pro and on an 18-task subset of Terminal-Bench 2.1, tracked during training.
Work per solved task (turns, visible content, reasoning and generated tokens) Medians per task, this adapter / the base model, over the tasks both solved: same tasks, same outcome, so the numbers measure only how much work each needed. Generated tokens are everything the model writes (visible content, reasoning and tool calls); content is the visible text between tool cal

models.readme_content:
--- license: apache-2.0 library_name: inworld-voice-isolation pipeline_tag: audio-to-audio tags: [audio, speech, speech-enhancement, speech-denoising, noise-suppression, voice-isolation, 48khz, full-band, streaming, realtime] ---

Voice Isolator

Open-license (Apache-2.0) 48 kHz voice isolation for noisy speech recordings and live audio.

--- ## TL;DR Inworld Voice Isolator v1 ships as two models that share one architecture: | | `voice-isolator-v1` | `voice-isolator-v1-realtime` | |---|---|---| | made for | recorded audio and anything not latency-sensitive, at the best quality | live audio, as a stream in your pipeline or production | | how it runs | offline: every frame sees its whole 8 s chunk | a causal stream with 20 ms of look-ahead | | parameters | 64M | 58M | **Use them for** cleaning recordings before playback or publication, curating speech datasets and voice pipelines where the speaker's identity must survive. With the realtime model, use them for live calls and streams. Subtract the isolated voice from the input to extract background noise or a backing-track residual for vocals/music separation. **They are not** a speaker selector or a restoration model. Restoration is planned for version 2 (see [Plans](https://github.com/inworld-ai/voice-isolator#plans)). ## Quick start Using a coding agent? Point it at the [setup section of AGENTS.md](https://github.com/inworld-ai/voice-isolator/blob/main/AGENTS.md#setting-up-the-voice-isolator-for-a-user): it installs the package, checks the machine with `voice-isolate-doctor` and cleans a first file. ```bash pip install inworld-voice-isolation # or from a clone: git clone https://github.com/inworld-ai/voice-isolator && cd voice-isolator && pip install -e . # a noisy example; a clone also has it at demo/examples/sample_14.wav curl -LO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/inworld-ai/voice-isolator/main/demo/examples/sample_14.wav # offline isolation (downloads the offline model on first use): # the voice goes to sample_14_clean.wav and the removed background # to sample_14_clean_background.wav, beside it voice-isolate sample_14.wav sample_14_clean.wav ``` Both are float32 WAVs at 48 kHz, with their original levels preserved; together they reconstruct the aligned mono input. Use `--output-sr 0` to keep the input rate, `--background noise.wav` to choose the background path for one file, or `--no-background` to save only the voice. ```python from inworld import voice_isolation # isolate a recording offline offline = voice_isolation.VoiceIsolator("inworld/voice-isolator") wav, sample_rate = voice_isolation.load_audio("sample_14.wav") voice = offline.isolate(wav, sample_rate) voice_isolation.save_audio("sample_14_clean.wav", voice, sample_rate, subtype="FLOAT") voice_isolation.save_audio("sample_14_clean_background.wav", wav - voice, sample_rate, subtype="FLOAT") # what was removed ``` ### Streaming The realtime model isolates the voice as the audio arrives, with 20 ms of look-ahead: ```python import torch from inworld import voice_isolation live = voice_isolation.VoiceIsolator("inworld/voice-isolator", mode="streaming", lookahead_frames=2) session = live.stream() # takes 48 kHz mono, in pieces of any size wav, sample_rate = voice_isolation.load_audio("sample_14.wav") # 48 kHz mono, standing in for a live source voice = [] for start in range(0, len(wav), 960): # 20 ms at a time, as a microphone delivers it voice.append(session.push(wav[start:start + 960])) # the samples that are final: play or send them voice.append(session.flush()) # the rest, once the source ends voice_isolation.save_audio("sample_14_streamed.wav", torch.cat(voice), sample_rate) ``` The streaming CLI writes only the isolated voice, after the whole file has gone through: ```bash voice-isolate sample_14.wav sample_14_streamed.wav --mode streaming --lookahead 2 ``` The weights download on first use, and their checksums are verified. The mode picks the checkpoint: `voice-isolator-v1` offline, `voice-isolator-v1-realtime` for streaming. CUDA is used when available, Apple's Metal backend (`mps`) on an Apple-silicon Mac with PyTorch 2.6 or later, and the CPU otherwise; `--device` picks one. The code, the [interactive demo](https://github.com/inworld-ai/voice-isolator/blob/main/demo/README.md) and the [benchmark](https://github.com/inworld-ai/voice-isolator/blob/main/bench/README.md) are on GitHub: [inworld-ai/voice-isolator](https://github.com/inworld-ai/voice-isolator). The demo loads both models at startup: **Offline** processes files and samples into voice and background audio; **Online** streams the microphone for up to 60 seconds with updating waveforms and spectrograms, pausing capture before playback. ## Hardware Tested on NVIDIA Ampere, Hopper and Blackwell GPUs (A100, H100, B200 and B300) and on CPU. Smaller GPUs are not tested yet (see [Plans](https://github.com/inworld-ai/voice-isolator#plans)). ## The VIBE benchmark

--- library_name: transformers license: apache-2.0 pipeline_tag: image-text-to-text --- # Qwen3.8-27B > [!Note] > This repository contains model weights and configuration files for the post-trained model in the Hugging Face Transformers format. > > These artifacts are compatible with Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, TokenSpeed, etc. > [!Tip] > For users seeking managed, scalable inference without infrastructure maintenance, the official Qwen API service is provided by [Qwen Cloud](https://www.qwencloud.com). > In particular, **Qwen3.8-27B** will be available as a hosted version with more production features, e.g., 1M context length by default, official built-in tools. For more information, please refer to the [Qwen3.8-27B Overview](https://www.qwencloud.com/models/qwen3.8-27b). The service is coming soon. Stay tuned for updates. Following the widespread community adoption of the Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6 series, we are pleased to introduce Qwen3.8, the most capable generation in the Qwen open-model family to date. Built on the architectural foundation of Qwen3.5, Qwen3.8 delivers substantial gains across coding, professional work, research, and long-horizon agentic tasks. Qwen3.8-27B brings these advances to a compact, deployment-friendly dense model: a native vision-language model that understands images and videos, with flexible thinking control, designed to carry complex, multi-step tasks through to completion with greater reliability. ## Qwen3.8 Highlights Qwen3.8-27B features the following enhancements: - **Core Capabilities**: Comprehensive improvements across coding, professional work, research, and long-horizon agentic tasks. - **Agent Execution**: Stronger autonomous planning and better handling of environment feedback, leading to more reliable end-to-end task completion. - **Downstream Compatibility**: Broader support for popular harnesses and development tools, making it easier to integrate into your existing stack. - **Flexible Thinking Control**: Thinking mode is on by default and can be disabled per request; reasoning depth can be tuned with `reasoning_effort`, and reasoning context from historical messages is retained via `preserve_thinking`. - **Vision-Language Understanding**: Native support for image and video understanding, from STEM diagrams and documents to hour-scale videos. ## Model Overview - Type: Causal Language Model with Vision Encoder - Training Stage: Pre-training & Post-training - Language Model - Number of Parameters: 27B - Hidden Dimension: 5120 - Token Embedding: 248,320 (Padded) - Number of Layers: 64 - Hidden Layout: 16 × (3 × (Gated DeltaNet → FFN) → 1 × (Gated Attention → FFN)) - Gated DeltaNet: - Number of Linear Attention Heads: 48 for V and 16 for QK - Head Dimension: 128 - Gated Attention: - Number of Attention Heads: 24 for Q and 4 for KV - Head Dimension: 256 - Rotary Position Embedding Dimension: 64 - Feed Forward Network: - Intermediate Dimension: 17,408 - LM Output: 248,320 (Padded) - MTP (Multi-Token Prediction): trained with multiple steps - Context Length: 262,144 natively and extensible up to 1,000,000 tokens. ## Benchmark Results ### Text Performance

# MiniMax-H3-Image ## Online API Use MiniMax-H3-Image directly via API. - Global: [platform.minimax.io](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/guides/image-generation) | CN: [platform.minimax.cn](https://platform.minimax.cn/docs/guides/image-generation) API docs: - Text-to-image: [EN-docs](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-generations), [CN-docs](https://platform.minimax.cn/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-generations) - Image editing: [EN-docs](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-edits), [CN-docs](https://platform.minimax.cn/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-edits) - Prompt expansion: [EN-docs](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-context-ir), [CN-docs](https://platform.minimax.cn/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-context-ir) ## Online App Use MiniMax-H3-Image directly via App. - WebApp Global: [hailuoai.video](https://hailuoai.video/) | CN: [hailuoai.com](https://hailuoai.com/) - Desktop Global: [agent.minimax.io](https://agent.minimax.io/) | CN: [agent.minimax.cn](https://agent.minimax.cn) ## Introduction MiniMax-H3-Image is a state-of-the-art open-source model for image generation and editing from the [MiniMax H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3) family. It combines intelligent understanding of creative intent with the ability to build visual worlds: with precise instruction following, it develops a creative concept into concrete characters, scenes and atmosphere. Generation and editing are unified in one checkpoint, which generates images from text (text-to-image) and edits one or more reference images (image editing), giving creators and developers a flexible and controllable way to create images. It generates images of about 16 megapixels at every aspect ratio, from 4096x4096 (1:1) to 6272x2688 (21:9), directly and without an upscaler (see [Sizes](#sizes)). The checkpoint is distilled to 6 sampling steps (6 NFEs) with no classifier-free guidance. Its diffusion transformer (DiT) has the H3 architecture without the audio layers, and it uses the MiniMax-H3 text encoder unchanged. ![Fifteen MiniMax-H3-Image text-to-image results in landscape and portrait formats: a 3D fantasy battle, a blue-green landscape painting, a tree frog, an indigo-dyed rabbit, a 3D white-haired girl, a portrait among flowers, a sci-fi city, dumplings, a highland cow, a mirror portrait, a 3D otter and sheep, a pixel art cat, a jewel beetle, giant cherries and a fisheye selfie](assets/showcase_hero.jpg) **Highlights** MiniMax-H3-Image brings together three core strengths: speed, image quality, and instruction following. 1. **16-megapixel images at a practical computational cost.** Compared with the 1–4 MP outputs common today, 16 MP (4096 × 4096) images offer far more detail but typically require substantially more computation. MiniMax-H3-Image keeps that computational cost manageable, making 16 MP generation practical for everyday creation. 2. **Rich detail. Remarkable realism.** MiniMax-H3-Image goes beyond the familiar “AI look” to produce images with intricate detail and lifelike realism, opening up more possibilities for creative and professional use. It brings generated imagery closer to the richness and nuance of the real visual world. 3. **Stronger instruction following.** Greater creative control. Great image generation goes beyond beautiful pictures—it helps creators bring their ideas to life. MiniMax-H3-Image delivers the strongest instruction following among open-source models and supports up to 16 reference images, giving creators more control over the final result. ## Model Zoo | Model | Role | Precision | Size | Hugging Face | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **MiniMax-H3-Image** | Text-to-image and image editing | BF16 (DiT) | 68.65 GB | [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxA

models.readme_content:
--- license: apache-2.0 pipeline_tag: text-generation tags: - moe - text-generation ---
📄 Technical Report  |   💬 GitHub

## 1. Model Introduction **Maxwell-V1.0-Flash** is a next-generation, high-performance Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model developed by the Maxwell Team, with **35B total parameters and 3B active parameters per token** (both excluding embeddings) and support for context lengths up to 256K tokens. It is designed for strong reasoning, agentic, and long-context capabilities at a practical inference cost.
Key Features
- **Maxwell Block Sparse Attention (MBSA).** Each KV group keeps fixed coverage of 8 prefix and 8 local 128-token blocks and adds up to 16 remote blocks chosen by a learned indexer, bounding main attention at 4,096 tokens per KV group while the full-history KV cache stays available. The MBSA kernel is 6.7x faster than dense GQA at 256K. - **Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections.** Multiple residual streams with learned, input-dependent aggregation and constrained mixing, widening information flow without extra attention or feed-forward evaluations. - **Fine-Grained Mixture of Experts.** A mostly-MoE backbone pairing fine-grained routed experts with always-active shared experts, using a dynamic routing correction bias alongside a lightweight sequence-wise load-balancing loss. **Pre-training.** Approximately **26T tokens** of multilingual data, with the Muon optimizer on most hidden weight matrices. Training starts dense; block-sparse attention enters at 128K mid-training, once the indexer is warmed up against dense full-history attention, then trains jointly with the backbone. **Tokenizer and Long Context.** A script-aware multilingual tokenizer stays compact across languages, especially low-resource Southeast Asian ones such as Thai, Lao, Myanmar, Khmer, and Shan. Long-context training then extends the sequence length in stages from 4K to 256K. **Post-training.** Two-stage all-domain SFT builds general, reasoning, and agentic capabilities, then targets harder reasoning problems and agent trajectories. Independent RL branches cover general tasks, verifiable reasoning (mathematics, science, logic, code), and agentic tasks (search, terminal use, function calling, software engineering). Multi-teacher on-policy distillation then merges them into one model by supervising student-generated responses. The results below summarize Maxwell-V1.0-Flash's performance across reasoning, agentic search, and other capabilities alongside the evaluated comparison models.

# ChatR Labs Uncensored Omni — Quantized

[![Try the Playground](https://img.shields.io/badge/Playground-Try_it_live-2563eb?style=for-the-badge)](https://chatrlabs.com/)
[![Base model](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hugging_Face-Base_model-ffcc4d?style=for-the-badge)](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1)
[![Chatr AI](https://img.shields.io/static/v1?label=CHATR%20AI&message=SUPPORT%20OUR%20RESEARCH&color=8B5CF6&labelColor=555555&style=for-the-badge)](https://thechatr.ai)

> **A special thank-you to [Chatr AI](https://thechatr.ai).** Training models requires significant computing resources, and Chatr AI generously provided the GPU infrastructure that made this release possible. If you would like to help us release more open-weight models, please support Chatr AI—their support directly powers our research and future community releases.

**Quantized builds at adapter weight 1.0, for text-to-image generation and image editing.**

This repository ships **quantized transformer weights only**. The model is our rank-128 Omni adapter merged into
[Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1) at **LoRA strength 1.0**, then quantized.
The text encoder, processor and VAE are not included; take them from the base repository.

File integrity information is in [SHA256SUMS](./SHA256SUMS).

### Which build should I use?

- **ComfyUI, one file, both workflows** -> any **GGUF**. It also loads in Diffusers via `from_single_file`.
- **ComfyUI, native quant ops** -> **FP8**, **INT8 ConvRot** or **NVFP4**.
- **Diffusers, smallest download** -> **NF4** (needs `bitsandbytes`).
- **Diffusers, best fidelity** -> **FP8 (torchao)** (needs `torchao`).
- **Maximum fidelity overall** -> **BF16 GGUF**, **BF16 safetensors** or **Q8_0**.
- **Diffusers without the `gguf` package** -> the **BF16** folder (plain `from_pretrained`).

The `297` and `265` layouts use different MLP representations: `265` uses the fused `img_mlp.gate_up`
projection; `297` keeps the separate `gate_layer` / `proj` pair. A loader must support the selected layout.
The BF16 ComfyUI workflow below was verified with the `297`-tensor safetensors file and the native
`UNETLoader` in ComfyUI 0.39.0; support should not be assumed for older or different loaders.

## Recommended settings

These are the values from our inference grid search for the non-distilled model.

| Setting | Starting value |
| --- | --- |
| Base components | Text encoder, processor and VAE from `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1` |
| Sampling steps | **35** |
| True CFG scale | **5.0** (both text-to-image and editing) |
| Sampler | `er_sde` with the `simple` scheduler (ComfyUI) |
| Negative prompt | A single space: `" "` |
| Output resolution | `768 x 1152` or `1024 x 1024` |
| KV cache | Enabled |

An omitted or empty negative prompt disables true CFG even when `true_cfg_scale` is greater than 1. Use a single
space if you do not need a specific negative prompt. This is a regular LoRA merge; it does not provide few-step
distillation.

## Usage with ComfyUI

```
ComfyUI/models/
|-- diffusion_models/    qwen-image-2.1-step90000-Q5_K_M.gguf
|-- text_encoders/       <Qwen-Image-2.1 text encoder>
`-- vae/                 <Qwen-Image-2.1 VAE>
```

- **GGUF:** `Unet Loader (GGUF)` -> pick the file. Works for both text-to-image and editing.
- **Comfy native:** `Load Diffusion Model` -> pick a `-comfy.safetensors` file.
- **Editing:** encode the reference image with `Text Encoder (Qwen-Image)` in edit mode; the latent comes from that node.
- Sampler: `er_sde`, scheduler `simple`, 35 steps, CFG 5.0.
